This is the SUPERVISED dual-domain U-Net (proj_dn -> FBP(full views) -> img_dn, MSE-vs-truth + lambda_neg negativity penalty), NOT the per-image N2I variant. SIZING: itnet_v3 (heavier -- k=3 unrolled DC steps) iter-1 trained 8 epochs + scored all 214 slices in 738s (~12.3 min) under this same sbatch wall; DD-UNet has no unrolled DC loop so it is CHEAPER per step -> 8 epochs + 214-slice per-sample val + figure fits comfortably inside the 20-min budget (30-min sbatch wall). HYPOTHESIS: dual_domain_supervised at c=16/lr=1e-4/ep=8 on ~200-400 stratified Mayo train slices trains stably (no NaN, grad-clip+skip holds) and produces a finite val_ssim that CLEARS the LD-FBP baseline (hr>0), because a supervised dual-domain (sinogram + image U-Net) denoiser of the full-view FBP is a strong Mayo recon family (loose hint from the discarded boundary-slice run: ~0.96 SSIM with epochs as the lever -- NOT a validated number under the corrected 214-slice 321px-FOV metric). This onboarding iter establishes the corrected-metric baseline that iter-2+ will improve by tuning ONE knob (epochs first, then lambda_neg).

HYPOTHESIS: epochs is still the lever; +35pct more gradient steps (20->27) lifts hr above the iter-2 0.338985 (predicted iter-3 hr ~0.36-0.38, extrapolating the iter1->iter2 +0.063/12-epoch slope, sub-linearly as convergence approaches). ONE KNOB: CAPACITY unet_c 16 -> 24 (the two SmallUNet denoisers proj_dn+img_dn both widen; params ~0.466M -> ~1.05M, a (24/16)^2=2.25x conv-compute bump), with epochs TRADED DOWN 27 -> 10 to fit the HARD 20-min (1200s) train+score wall. SIX-BOX. (1) NUMBERS: iter-2 ep20/c16 SSIM 0.909762 hr 0.338985; iter-3 ep27/c16 SSIM 0.918191 hr 0.365357 (CHAMPION) in elapsed_s=1151.4; current config unet_c=16 epochs=27 lr=1e-4. (2) LIMITER: the epochs lever WORKS (monotone hr ep8 0.276 -> ep20 0.339 -> ep27 0.3654) but is now WALL-LOCKED: iter-3 ep27 used 1151.4s of the 1200s budget; the iter-3 note computed ep32 -> 1366s BUSTS the wall, so epochs cannot rise. The other budget-free lever, an lr-schedule, is NOT WIRED in solver_dual_ddomain_supervised.py (opt=torch.optim.Adam(lr=cfg['lr']) at line 151, no scheduler/weight_decay) and adding one would require editing a SHARED solver (FORBIDDEN). So the only legitimate single-knob iter-4 lever is CAPACITY (unet_c, wired at line 141 -> both denoisers). Is the champion capacity-limited? iter-3's own falsifier said 'if hr <= 0.339 at ep27 -> capacity-limited'; hr ROSE to 0.3654 instead, so it is still PARTLY training-limited, NOT cleanly capacity-limited -> trading epochs down is a genuine gamble, which is exactly what this iter tests. (3) ONE KNOB: unet_c 16->24, epochs 27->10. BUDGET-TRADE MATH: from the two measured c16 points per_epoch=(893.06-418.58)/(20-8)=39.5s/epoch, fixed (data load + 214-slice per-sample val + figure I/O)=418.58-8*39.5=102.6s (iter-3 ep27 predicted 1169s vs actual 1151.4s, calibration good). A c16->c24 widening multiplies the U-Net portion of compute by (24/16)^2=2.25x; the per-sample 2304-view FBP adjoint is c-INDEPENDENT, so the REALISTIC per-epoch at c24 (assuming ~30pct of per-epoch is the c-independent FBP adjoint) is 39.5*(0.30+0.70*2.25)=74.1s and realistic fixed (val ~half c-scaling) ~166s -> ep10 realistic = 166+10*74.1=908s (~15.1 min, comfortably inside 1200s). The WORST-CASE upper bound (pessimistically assume EVERYTHING incl. the FBP adjoint scales 2.25x): per_epoch_worst=39.5*2.25=89.0s, fixed_worst=102.6*2.25=230.9s -> ep10 worst = 230.9+10*89.0=1120s < 1200s -> FITS even the worst case. ep12 worst=1298s BUSTS, so without a measured c24 timing point ep10 is the LARGEST epoch count guaranteed to fit; epochs is sized to the worst-case bound, not the optimistic one (a wall-bust wastes the whole QOS slot). (4) HYPOTHESIS: 2.25x more representational capacity lifts hr above the iter-3 champion 0.365357 even at the reduced ep10, because the DD-UNet is a strong recon family and the discarded boundary-slice run loosely hinted c=24 was its best capacity (TPE: c=24, ep=18, hr 0.836 under that bad metric -- behavior hint only). FALSIFIER (in NUMBERS): if hr <= 0.365 at unet_c=24/ep10, the DD-UNet has hit its representational ceiling on this val set (~0.37) AND/OR ep10 under-trained the bigger net more than the capacity helped -> document the champion ceiling; iter-5 would then either (a) keep c24 and recover epochs toward the wall if c24 per-epoch is measured to be cheaper than the worst case (i.e. ep10 left budget headroom), or (b) revert to c16/ep27 and accept 0.3654 as the DD-UNet ceiling. (5) HARD 20-min train+score budget; val=ALL 214 L277 slices; grad_clip=1.0 (mandatory; the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint amplifies gradients ~18x -> lr kept conservative at 1e-4 + nonfinite-grad-skip). (6) no control return.
